To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a combined RNA extraction and selective amplification protocol to obtain Brucella melitenesis total RNA from mixed host-pathogen samples.
we describe an efficient protocol for the preparation of Brucella total RNA from a host:pathgen mixed sample, which is suitable for downstream gene expression analysis.
we developed a combined protocol for the preparation of Brucella RNA, which is suitable for gene expression analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an RNA isolation protocol for the study of Brucella gene expression.

the development of a new method for the selective amplification of Br. melitensis transcripts, which can be applied to a variety of experimental models and can be easily adapted to the amplification of other prokaryotic pathogens.
the study of the host-pathogen interaction in Brucella infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method we describe here allows analysis of B. melitenis gene expression profiles in the presence of limited amounts of host RNA.

the protocol presented here provides a novel and effective method to enrich Brucella RNA and to selectively amplify Brucella transcripts from a mixed host:pathogen RNA sample, thus facilitating the study of the pathogen transcriptome during host:pathogen interaction.
the protocol described in this manuscript allows the selective amplification of Br. melitensis mRNA when limited amounts of total RNA are present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this protocol allows the selective amplification of Br. melitensis mRNA and is a powerful tool to analyze the transcriptome of intracellular B. species.
we have developed a method to obtain Brucella RNA from a host:pathgen mixed RNA sample that can be used for further analysis of Brucella gene expression.

the combination of the two methods described here allows the selective amplification of Br. melitensis mRNA and its subsequent use in downstream applications, such as microarrays or quantitative RT-PCR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protocol described here can be used to obtain good quality RNA from a pathogen present in very small amounts in a mixed sample.
it is possible to obtain a sufficient quantity and quality of Brucella mRNA from a mixed RNA sample to perform downstream analysis, even when the pathogen is present in very low numbers.
the combined protocol allows the selective amplification of Br. melitensis mRNA, and that this is possible even with low quantities of Br. melitenesis mRNA in a host-pathogen mixed sample.
